newsitem.title: USA: Summers expects debt relief agreement at IMF.
newsitem.headline: Summers expects debt relief agreement at IMF.

text.p: A senior U.S. official said Thursday he expects agreement at the upcoming IMF/World Bank annual meeting on a multilateral debt relief initiative for poor countries.
"I expect an agreement on the outline of an initiative for the highly-indebted poor countries," Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers told Financial Times television.
Summers said the agreement would involve action by the Paris Club, the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and regional development banks.
Summers' comments suggested that the Paris Club of creditor nations had agreed to go along with the initiative at a meeting Thursday.
But he declined comment when asked by reporters about any Paris Club agreement.

To help finance its participation in the debt relief initiative the IMF will need to sell some of its gold holdings, Summers said. "It's clear at this point, that down the road, in order to finance the commitments that have been made, the sale of gold will be necessary."

U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin seemed to suggest earlier on Thursday that a gold sale decision might not be necessary until the year 2000. But U.S. officials indicated that a decision would have to come earlier than that.
Rubin will be meeting fellow finance ministers from the Group of Seven major industrial nations Saturday on the fringes of the IMF/World Bank annual meetings.
Asked what the agenda of the G7 meeting will be, Summers replied "we'll be doing what we usually do."
That means taking stock of the world economy. "Obviously it will be important to keep the momentum of economic growth in place in both Europe and Japan."
